title.narrative: Strengthening food and nutrition security in rural households in Southeast, Liberia through LANN+

description.narrative: Measures Direct project participants Indirect project participants. Target 1: 500 smallholder farmers have increased their crop production and reduced post-harvest losses.Target 2: 200 mothers from the target communities have improved their knowledge of nutrition, child care, hygiene and sanitation practices.Target 3: Improve community income generation and access to credit for 500 smallholder farmers. Target 4: VOSIEDA has improved its operational capacity and expertise for the sustainable implementation of current and future projects. Total Direct: 710.Total Indirect: 52.550

Overall objective: Sustainably improving food and nutrition security for vulnerable households in rural counties of Montserrado and Grand BassaProject Objective: 700 project participants (500 smallholder farmers and 200 mothers) and their family members have sustainably diversified their diets and improved their nutritional status

The LANN+ approach used this project is based on the UNICEF model, which divides the causes of food and nutrition insecurity into three categories: the immediate causes, which relate to direct factors such as the diet and health of the individual; the underlying causes, which include household and community factors such as access to food, care practices, and health services; as well as the fundamental causes, which encompass broader social, economic, and political structures that influence the underlying conditions. As a result, the LANN+ approach allows for a comprehensive view and consideration of all factors that contribute to food and nutrition insecurity.
